newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Fujimori urges no ransom payments.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Fujimori urges no ransom payments.

text.p: Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori urged Japanese firms on Wednesday not to pay ransoms to Marxist guerrillas holding their representatives hostage at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.
"I hope that these companies do not give in to their pressures," Fujimori told reporters.
The Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) is holding about a dozen Japanese businessmen among 74 hostages still being held at the residence.

Although the MRTA has in the past kidnapped businessmen and politicians to raise money, there has been no evidence that this was their aim in the current crisis. Their principal demand has been the release of about 400 jailed comrades.
Fujimori also addressed a crowd in a Lima shantytown, where he was greeted with cheers and chants of "We are with you."
"There is no MRTA follower here," Fujimori told the crowd. "You have suffered violence...We are not going to allow the terrorists to continue killing."
